auditLogFragment.purpose: docs/FAIL_OPEN_PLAN.md R2: real in-git example of a top-level `fragments` entry, mirroring the shape of AppGen/apps/npdev_split_model_sample_app's plugin/sendMail.json fragment (capabilities + bindings + metadata, $ref-ed from model.json).
auditLogFragment.correction2026_08_19: The original binding pointed 'auditLog' at adapter 'audit-log-inproc' -- a builtin-style name that mimics real registered adapters (mail-inproc, notification-inproc, webhook-inproc) but was never actually registered in NPDevGenerator/resources/Plugins/{default,dev}.plugin-manifest.json, and no such adapter class ever existed under NPDevKernel/adapters. NpdevCapabilityBindingConfig.capabilityRegistry() (NPDevRuntimeHost) eagerly resolves EVERY declared binding against RuntimePluginAdapterRegistry at boot, so the generated app failed to start with 'Adapter audit-log-inproc for capability auditLog ... is not declared in active plugin manifest' even though nothing ever called it. This was a fixture defect, not a generator/runtime defect -- no real app author naming a real capability collides with this made-up name. Fixed by switching the binding to the genuine 'plugin:java-source' mounted-capability mechanism (same one proven live by NPDevSamples/probes/lib-probe's librarySignature capability): a capability.plugin.json descriptor + real Java source under capabilities/auditLog/, and a RecordAuditLogEntry flow so CompiledPluginRequirementGraphBuilder actually discovers the requirement and GeneratedPluginMountPlan mounts it -- an unreferenced binding is never mounted, flow call or not.
